newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy ends mixed, July down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy ends mixed, July down on profit-taking.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended mixed Monday, with July under pressure from traders taking profits on the July/November spread, floor sources said.
"Today the July/Nov (spread) was the story," said Ron Kucha, trader with O'Connor and Co. Grain in Chicago.
Profit taking on the old crop/new crop soybean spread was triggered by talk that the soybean basis had softened enough in Brazil to spur imports to the U.S., traders said.
Supplies of U.S. old crop soybeans are tight and expensive because farmers are focusing on planting rather than marketing what is left of their crops, traders said.
New crop soybeans were up on ideas that heavy rains in the eastern Corn Belt might mean that farmers would have to delay replanting in already saturated fields, agronomists said.
Weekly export inspections of 7.897 million bushels fell at the low end of trade expectations for seven million to 11 million bushels and also pressed July, traders said.
On the day, Smith Barney bought one million bushels November, three million August and three million July. Refco sold five million July and 1.5 million November.
CBOT soybeans settled 5-1/4 cents per bushel lower to eight cents per bushel up, with July down 5-1/4 at $8.75-1/4.
Most of the soybean crop has been planted. Traders were looking for the USDA's crop progress report to show the U.S. soybean crop 80 to 85 percent planted.
Some bearish traders warned that new crop contracts might start to tumble when the unwinding of bull spreads stops because U.S. weather for soybean devlopment was generally favorable.
"The soybeans need heat, and temperatures in the west are more like summer," a trader said.
High temperatures in the western Corn Belt were forecast to climb into the upper 70s (degrees Fahrenheit) to mid-80s on Monday, according to data supplied by Weather Express in Omaha, Neb.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 71,000 contracts. That figure compared with Friday's actual volume of 62,593.
